note: Hand labels for the two self-recorded demo calls, written by listening/reading the actual call against its script and the CRM/rate card fixture. Not the intended script outcome: what a human reviewer would actually mark, given what was actually said. Synthetic leads, no real customer (D17).

notes.recording_disclaimer: Agent gives the disclaimer at 12.4s, before any personal data is collected. Wording is a close paraphrase of the checklist text, not verbatim. A human reviewer would call this a clean PASS on substance even though the automated score sits at REVIEW (score 82, just under the 88 PASS threshold): this is the one place the model is stricter than a human would be.
notes.account_holder_confirmation: The agent asks 'can I confirm you are the account holder', which is a real account-holder confirmation in substance, but reads nothing like the checklist's exact phrasing derived from the CIMET transcript. A human reviewer familiar with the checklist would likely also flag this as not matching the approved script, so FAIL is defensible, though a lenient reviewer could argue REVIEW.
notes.plan_key_information: The CIS-style plan read is present but compressed; several required sentences (month-to-month terms, the explicit ongoing price restatement) are missing or paraphrased away. FAIL on substance, not just wording.
notes.total_minimum_cost_disclosed: The total minimum cost sentence is not said at all in this recording. Clear FAIL.
notes.ongoing_monthly_price: Agent states 79.90 twice; the rate card says 72.90. This is the deliberate script fault. Clear FAIL.
notes.customer_email: Agent reads back j.avery@example.com; CRM holds jordan.avery@example.com. Deliberate script fault. Clear FAIL.
notes.modem_model: The modem is named correctly (Netcomm CF40) but the line lands on a customer-attributed turn under speaker alignment (D18), so the automated check finds no agent-side mention and REVIEWs. A human listening to the audio would hear the agent say it and PASS this. This is the review's known false REVIEW, not a real content problem.

notes.ongoing_monthly_price: Scripted and spoken correctly: 72.90 is the only ongoing figure said in this call. The automated FAIL is a known false positive: a long merged turn under speaker alignment (D18) confuses the promo-vs-ongoing role tagger into reading the promo mention as a second, conflicting ongoing claim. A human listening to the audio hears one correct figure and would PASS this.
notes.promo_monthly_price: Same root cause as ongoing_monthly_price: the correct 42.90 promo figure is said once, correctly, but the same merged-turn confusion produces a false FAIL.
notes.total_minimum_cost_disclosed: The total minimum cost sentence is said in full and correctly in the recording. The automated FAIL traces to the same long merged turn: the sentence is present in the transcript but the coverage matcher's evidence window does not land cleanly on it inside that turn.
notes.customer_email: priya.shah@example.com is read back correctly and matches the CRM record exactly. The automated REVIEW happens because the email sentence sits inside the same long merged turn (70.6s-123.0s) and the span-isolation extractor does not find it there; the extractor is not wrong about what it can see, it simply cannot see this particular sentence inside that turn.
